title: Mistral Health - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery call focused on Mistral Health's requirements for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. Primary concerns: cross-account VPC connectivity, IP CIDR overlap, private endpoints, region constraints for HIPAA data residency, and KMS integration. Discussed options (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, AWS PrivateLink), expected traffic patterns, and next steps: send network diagram template, security docs, and schedule an SRE-led deep-dive with sample benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, th-thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya is our SE, she'll cover the network bits. Alex, do you want to kick off with your goals?
[00:18] Alex Romero: Yeah thanks. So Mistral's exploring a private deployment of Redwood, mostly for PHI workflows. Our big asks: run in our VPC or at least private endpoints, keys in our KMS, audit logs, and meet HIPAA residency — primarily us-east-1 and eu-west-1. We're worried about cross-account peering and overlap, we've got multiple accounts.
[00:38] Priya Nandakumar: Great, agree. So we typically support three patterns: peered VPC (cross-account VPC peering), Transit Gateway hub, or PrivateLink / interface endpoints. Each has tradeoffs around egress, DNS, and scaling.
[00:55] Dana Chen: Right — our infra team prefers PrivateLink for security but worried about throughput and cost. Can Redwood run high-throughput inference over PrivateLink?
[01:10] Priya Nandakumar: For steady high-throughput, Transit Gateway or dedicated VPC peering to Redwood's private deployment tends to be better. PrivateLink works but you need to watch ENI quotas and per-connection throughput — can be a bottleneck for batch workloads. Also cost-wise, PrivateLink egress is charged differently.
[01:32] Michael Park: For compliance, we need customer-managed KMS. Does Redwood support CMEK/HSM? Also, audit logs need to be forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support KMS integration in the Private offering; HSM integrations on request (we've done AWS CloudHSM for other customers). Audit logs and request traces can be exported to an S3 or pushed via syslog; we'll share the schema.
[02:02] Leah Ortiz: On CIDR space: we have overlapping /16 ranges across some business units, so peering might be problematic. What does Redwood suggest?
[02:16] Priya Nandakumar: Overlap is the classic problem. Options: use NATing on your side and route through a Transit Gateway with route translations, or deploy a dedicated VPC in a non-overlapping CIDR that you peer with. We can also run in a customer-managed VPC in a different account to avoid overlap.
[02:36] Alex Romero: Could you run in our account? We prefer everything in-house, but concerned about ops overhead.
[02:45] Carlos Mendes: We offer two private modes: Redwood-managed private (Redwood runs the control plane but data plane is in your VPC via peering/PrivateLink) and fully customer-hosted (we provide an on-prem/VPC package you deploy). The managed option reduces your ops burden.
[03:05] Dana Chen: If you run in our VPC, how do upgrades and rollback work? We need canary/partial rollouts.
[03:13] Priya Nandakumar: Same rollout model applies — we can support canary policies by model version and route a subset of traffic to new models. For customer-hosted we provide the orchestration manifests and can run X% traffic to a canary via routing policies. There are some network considerations when routing across accounts but that's manageable.
[03:33] Michael Park: Latency SLAs — what's realistic from us-east-1 to a Redwood-managed private deployment in the same region?
[03:42] Jordan Lee: If everything is co-located in us-east-1 and using peering or Transit Gateway, p95 latency for short prompts is typically sub-100ms for our optimized models, but depends on model size and batch behavior. For bursty traffic, batching can increase throughput but adds a few tens of ms.
[04:00] Alex Romero: We have workflows that are really latency-sensitive — inference under 150ms p95. Can you guarantee that?
[04:08] Priya Nandakumar: We offer latency SLOs for Dedicated pockets; for Private deployments we'd work to baseline with a pilot — if you need strict guarantees, Dedicated with reserved capacity is the right path. We'll propose a benchmark plan.
[04:24] Dana Chen: About DNS — will calls resolve to private IPs? How does service discovery work?
[04:30] Carlos Mendes: We support private DNS entries; we can either publish Route53 private hosted zones into your account or you can use endpoints and route via NLBs. If you're using PrivateLink, you'll get interface endpoints with private DNS integrated.
[04:45] Leah Ortiz: What about cross-region replication — we need eu-west-1 for EU patient data. Can we have a multi-region footprint pinned to specific models?
[04:54] Priya Nandakumar: Absolutely, you can pin model versions to regions. We can spin up deployments in multiple regions and route by policy based on data residency. That will increase cost, and we recommend warm standby in the secondary region to meet RTOs.
[05:12] Alex Romero: Any gotchas around egress IPs for allowlisting to our datastore?
[05:18] Priya Nandakumar: If Redwood manages the egress, we'll provide a list of egress IPs or NAT gateways. For customer-hosted, egress is under your control so you can keep fixed IPs. When using PrivateLink, traffic stays inside the AWS network, but outbound to other services will follow your VPC's egress paths.
[05:36] Michael Park: For audits we need SOC2 and pen-test reports.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: We'll share our SOC2 attestation and recent pen-test summary; for customer-hosted setups you get an additional HLD and deployment hardening guide.
[05:50] Alex Romero: What about SSO for access to the Redwood console — we need SAML and SCIM to manage groups.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning plus RBAC scoped to teams. In Private deployments we can either integrate with your IdP directly or proxy auth through the private control plane.
[06:11] Dana Chen: Ok, sounds good. Next, can we get a network template and a sample Terraform module?
[06:19] Carlos Mendes: Yes — action: we'll send network diagram template and sample Terraform for PrivateLink/Transit Gateway setup. Also will include KMS/HSM integration steps and the recommended CIDR ranges.
[06:30] Leah Ortiz: We'd also like to run a short benchmark — 48-72 hour run hitting our common prompts to measure p95 and cost.
[06:40] Priya Nandakumar: We'll draft a benchmark plan: sample prompts, expected QPS, model configs, and measurement metrics.
[06:47] Alex Romero: Great. Who's the main point for the SRE deep dive?
[06:51] Jordan Lee: Priya will lead the SRE deep dive; Carlos will own delivering the network artifacts. I'll follow up with pricing and next steps.
[07:00] (crosstalk)
[07:05] Jordan Lee: Quick recap — deliverables: network template + Terraform module, security docs (SOC2/pen-test), benchmark plan, SRE deep-dive scheduled next week. I'll send calendar invites. Anything else?
[07:20] Michael Park: Please include expected costs for PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway options.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[07:28] Alex Romero: Thanks, bye.

Share SOC2 attestation and pen-test summary (Jordan)
Schedule SRE deep-dive to run network/latency tests next week (Jordan/Priya)
Include cost comparison for PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway (Jordan)
